title: INT8/FP8 calibration and validation for reranker: automated profile sweep and NDCG/MRR gating
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: produce validated INT8 and experimental FP8 quantization profiles for the production reranker model (arch: two-tower cross-encoder) with an automated calibration sweep and a reproducible ranking-quality evaluation harness. Deliverables: 1) per-layer quantization profiles (scheme, scale, clip thresholds) tested against FP16 baseline; 2) an automated calibration workflow that picks best profile by NDCG@10 and MRR on standard holdout; 3) CI gating rules and fallback strategy if quality regresses. Approach: - Calibration: collect activation statistics from a stratified calibration corpus (50k queries with target documents representing high/medium/low relevance). Evaluate per-channel symmetric and asymmetric scales, per-tensor fallback for attention kernels, and experiment with power-of-two scaling vs learned scaling. - Outlier handling: compare min-max clipping, percentile clipping (99.9/99.5), and dynamic range reduction using KL-divergence calibration. - FP8 experiments: use FP8 hybrid (mantissa-exp bias tuning) on select dense layers where INT8 causes >0.5% NDCG drop. - Automation: build a sweep job that generates candidate profiles, runs a fast validation suite (10k queries) and then a full validation (50k queries) computing NDCG@1/3/10, MRR, and pairwise win-rate vs FP16. - Acceptance criteria: NDCG@10 drop <= 1.0% relative to FP16 AND MRR change within +/-0.75%. If thresholds fail, profile marked for manual review with per-layer attribution report. - Rollout plan: Canaries at 2% traffic with realtime monitoring (latency, token-cost), automatic rollback on quality regression, and opt-in experiment flags for dedicated customers. Integrations: artifact links, CI job names, and rollout policies are to be committed in the runtime-1.20 release branch.
